references.text: The parallel passage in the Gospel of Mark where the disciples admire the temple's stones and buildings, and Jesus responds by prophesying the temple's destruction. [ref:Mark 13:1-2|Markus 13:1-2]

The parallel passage in the Gospel of Matthew where the disciples show Jesus the temple's buildings, and Jesus prophesies that not one stone will be left upon another. [ref:Matt 24:1-2|Matteus 24:1-2]
The immediately following verse where Jesus responds to the admiration of the temple by prophesying its complete destruction. [ref:Luk 21:6|Lukas 21:6]

The description of the rebuilt temple after the exile, where the elders wept while the young shouted for joy – a testimony to the temple's significance and splendor in Israel's history. [ref:Esra 3:12|Esra 3:12]
Haggai's question about who remembered the temple in its former glory, highlighting the temple's splendor and its importance to the people. [ref:Hag 2:3|Haggai 2:3]

The Jews mention that the temple was built over 46 years, underscoring its grandeur and the immense effort invested in its construction – the same temple referred to in [ref:Luk 21:5|Lukas 21:5]. [ref:Joh 2:20|Johannes 2:20]
The description of Solomon's temple construction with precisely cut stones, pointing to the tradition of adorning the temple with costly stones. [ref:1 Kong 6:7|1. Kongebok 6:7]
The description of Solomon's temple adorned with gold, illustrating the tradition of decorating God's house with precious materials and gifts (ἀναθήμασιν). [ref:1 Kong 6:21-22|1. Kongebok 6:21-22]
The temple was decorated with gemstones, illustrating the tradition of adorning it with costly stones and votive offerings. [ref:2 Krøn 3:6|2. Krønikebok 3:6]
